newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - Minas and Duri crude overhang.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - Minas and Duri crude overhang.

text.p: Asian crude prices are expected to start the week on a weak tone after new-month trading kicked off last week.

An overhang of Minas and Duri is likely to plague the regional heavy sweet market after last month's 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) Dumai refinery turnaround and the unexpected stoppage of the 125,000 bpd Balongan refinery.
Traders said anything up to one million barrels each of Minas and Duri were overhanging the April market which, they said, indicates a market which will achieve flat to discounted differentials.
However, much will depend on China's appetite for the crude and also how Indonesia's Pertamina manages the stock during the trading month.
One trader said he would expect the state-owned oil firm to make a normal allocation of Minas for export of around 70,000 bpd. But that would still leave the million barrels in storage, he said.

Last month Pertamina initially allocated 94,300 bpd for March trading, higher than a normal allocation of around 70,000 bpd, but less than had been expected in view of the Dumai and Balongan situation.
"So long as it does not get shown, it should not weigh on the market too much," one trader said of the April market.
China purchased more than one million barrels of Minas crude late in the March trading month, indicating a possible appetite for the crude after Chinese buyers had been dormant for much of the month.
One Chinese buyer said he would wait for the Pertamina allocations early this week to assess the market.

Duri is also expected to have an overhang of a million barrels in April, but a trader said he would expect Pertamina to try to push some of that overhang into the export allocations. He estimated April allocations would be around 70,000 bpd, compared to a more normal allocation of about 30/40,000 bpd.
First indication on the sales of May Middle East grades has been bearish.
One million barrels of Oman traded into China at two cents above its official selling price (OSP), but then drifted to flat, traders said.
Market talk of Murban trading at a discount of 15 cents under its OSP were denied by the seller.
Refinery turnarounds in the region would still affect the market, with some Japanese refineries slating turnarounds heading into June.
However, most South Korean turnarounds scheduled for May and June are finished by the last week of June.

Traders said West African crude imports would play a major role also amid the weakness of the Brent market. However, so far, traders said imports only seemed to be moderate with most heading to the U.S..
